trend.title: Cushman & Wakefield: U.S. Industrial Vacancy Falls to 6.8% in Q3 2026 as Net Absorption Hits 76.6 Million Square Feet
trend.scope: U.S. industrial and logistics real estate (Cushman & Wakefield Q3 2026 U.S. Industrial MarketBeat)
trend.metric: 6.8% national industrial vacancy, 20 bps below the late-2025 peak; 76.6 msf Q3 net absorption
trend.summary: Cushman & Wakefield's Q3 2026 U.S. Industrial MarketBeat put national industrial vacancy at 6.8%, 20 basis points below its late-2025 peak and the lowest since year-end 2024. Net absorption reached 76.6 million square feet in the quarter, the strongest since the first quarter of 2023. The construction pipeline rose 6% from the second quarter to about 324 million square feet, up 23% year over year, and annual asking rent growth reached 4% nationwide. Data center-related users accounted for more than 8% of new leasing activity so far this year.
trend.significance: Falling vacancy and re-accelerating rents shift leverage to industrial landlords, raising the stakes in renewal-option and fair-market-rent resets, holdovers, expansion and right-of-first-offer disputes, and assignments by tenants trying to keep below-market leases. A rebuilding construction pipeline weighted toward build-to-suit projects brings more development-agreement, delay and mechanics' lien disputes, and data center-related users add zoning and power-supply questions to industrial siting.
